acceptedInterpretation: The single accepted reading: B-623a adds PUSH-based host burn detection on two advisory-only surfaces without any gate. (1) lattice doctor gains a Host burn scan (advisory) section that reuses the existing read-only core/usage-sweep.ts scanners (sweepCodexSessions/sweepClaudeProjects) over a recent-activity window and prints, per flagged session, a prominent warning naming the session file path, its cwd, and its cumulative input tokens plus which thresholds tripped. (2) usage_sweep gains an opt-in --alert flag that appends the same evaluation and makes the CLI exit non-zero when any session is flagged (recover_evidence dispatch pattern: full report printed first, then throw) so a cron can drive notifications. A session is flagged, strictly-greater than threshold, on any of three reasons matching the user example: transcript file size > 100MB, cumulative input tokens > 100M (Codex = last cumulative total_token_usage.input which already includes cache; Claude = summed input+cacheRead+cacheCreation, the cache-inclusive analogue), or session firstTimestamp older than 7 days while still recently active. These are DEFAULTS only, env-tunable via LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_FILE_MB / _INPUT_TOKENS / _AGE_DAYS / _RECENT_HOURS (48h scan window; 0 disables the doctor scan), with non-finite/negative/zero values falling back to the default (RECENT_HOURS=0 the sole intentional disable sentinel). The recent-mtime requirement is honored by the sweep sinceMs=now-recentHours window itself, so an old-but-still-open thread (old firstTimestamp, recently bumped mtime) is exactly what gets caught; the doctor push scan is deliberately bounded to that recent-activity window for all three reasons (doctor must stay fast), while unbounded historical scanning remains available through usage_sweep --since. Everything stays advisory-only and report-only per the B-70e9 non-goals: no gate wiring, hostBurnScan.gateEvidence=false, zero writes to the transcript stores, no host-session mutation, no usage-ledger coupling, and plain doctor / plain usage_sweep exit codes and dispatch stay byte-identical (only explicit --alert exits non-zero). The 100M default is retained verbatim; the empirical addendum recommending 50M is operator ADVICE only and does not change the frozen default.
notes: Checked: (a) thresholds 100MB/100M/7d are DEFAULTS with env tuning (CHK-002) matching the user example verbatim; default deliberately kept at 100M despite the addendum recommending 50M (advice not default) - no drift. (b) advisory-only boundary preserved: decision principles + plan + CHK-003 assert no gate, gateEvidence=false, plain exit codes unchanged; classification untouched (no ownership-gate/activity-policy edits), verified against F-014/F-028 read-only-regression pre-mortem. (c) --alert is opt-in exit-nonzero for cron via the recover_evidence print-then-throw pattern; plain sweep byte-identical (CHK-004). (d) warning names session file + cwd + cumulative tokens (CHK-003 userSees) - all three required fields present, extra fields (first/last activity, tripped thresholds) are enrichment not scope drift. (e) age>7d-with-recent-mtime honored via sweep sinceMs mtime window - verified in core/usage-sweep.ts lines 146-150 (mtime kept authoritative so still-active old threads are retained), matching the user motivating case (month-old but still-open 019e40d0 / 9 concurrently-open threads). Near-misses considered and cleared: (1) Claude token formula includes cacheRead+cacheCreation whereas the user quoted only Codex total_token_usage.input - cleared because usage-sweep.ts line 24 confirms Codex cumulative already includes cache, so the Claude summed-with-cache formula is the consistent cross-host analogue, not a broadening. (2) doctor bounding ALL three reasons to a 48h window could narrow the literal unconditional file>100MB / input>100M clauses - cleared because the burn intent targets ACTIVELY re-paying threads (recent mtime), the window is env-tunable, and unbounded historical scans remain in usage_sweep --since; not an intent-defeating narrowing. No omissions: doctor check, scanner reuse, read-only, three thresholds, env-tunable, --alert cron mode, and advisory-only all present.
